# Hardening audit and sprint plan

Branch `feature/uploader-hardening` @ `f146588`. Audit date 2026-07-29.

Ten parallel read-only audits covering: core write-path concurrency, the two engine plugins, API and
security surface, the React client, CLI and deploy shell, test quality, docs correctness,
Swarm and hls.js library capability, architecture and patterns, and silent failures.

Scope audited: ~5,900 lines of TypeScript, ~1,780 lines of shell, plus compose files and templates.

## Definition of done, and the only queue that counts

**Owner decision, 2026-08-01. This section outranks everything below it.** A later session reads this
first and works nothing else without asking.

### Done

> A live stream survives a publisher reconnect, an uploader crash, and a Bee outage without losing a
> VOD or leaking a puller, and an operator can tell when it does not.

That is the whole bar. **The register being empty is not the bar and never was.**

### Why this exists

Measured on 2026-08-01 across the two pull requests of that day: **379 lines of process documentation,
367 lines of tests, 99 lines of product source.** Nearly four lines of process for every line of the
system. Eight findings opened, two closed. The register stood at 124 rows and 23 open HIGHs.

Three things were compounding.

**The review protocol became a workstream rather than a control.** A change to make reviews cheaper was
itself gated, that gate found three HIGHs in the new rules, and correcting them produced more rules.
`review-gate.md` is longer than most of the code it governs.

**The register has no drain.** Every round opened more rows than its fix closed, so a document meant to
track work became a document that generates it.

**One severity ladder served both the product and the paperwork.** "The guard silently drops real
closings and never publishes a VOD" and "fail-closed cannot fire on a deferred lens" were both HIGH.
That is how documentation outweighed source four to one, because the doc work genuinely felt as urgent.

The sharpest evidence is in this file: **CON-21 is marked CLOSED and CON-22, CON-23 and CON-24 are all
about the same guard.** The fix renamed the problem into three.

### The target is the sprint plan again, batched

**Owner decision, 2026-08-01, superseding the seven-row queue below.** The queue was a narrowing, and
it worked: CON-22 and CON-23 went from nothing to a gated pull request in one session. What it did not
fix is the cost per unit of work. Measured the same day: **six sprint IDs across 257 commits, 14 of 48
sprint tasks done.** The plan stopped driving the work on about day two and the gate's own findings
drove it instead.

So the target is the full [sprint plan](#sprint-plan) again, with three changes to how it is worked.

1. **Batch by theme, not by task.** One pull request per cluster of related tasks, not one per task.
   S4.3, S4.4, S4.7 and S4.8 are four shell fixes and one pull request. S1.5 through S1.7 are one. The
   per-round cost barely depends on the size of the change, so 34 remaining tasks become roughly ten to
   twelve pull requests rather than thirty-four.
2. **Gate at sprint boundaries, not per pull request.** Per pull request the check is `pnpm verify` and
   `pnpm audit:check` in CI, which is a machine and produces no findings to triage. The lens round and
   the Stryker run happen once per sprint over that sprint's whole diff.
3. **At a sprint gate a finding is fixed in that sprint, archived on sight, or moved to the
   live-infrastructure block below, and that third destination is owner-added only.** A row enters it
   only when the specific assertion no fake can make is named. "Easier with a live engine" does not
   qualify, and neither does a row a session would rather not do. Without that gate the block is the
   "we will get to it" tier this rule was written to abolish, and any row can reach it by being
   described as needing a stack.
   The rule as first written said there is no third tier at all, which the block then contradicted
   forty lines later in this same file.
   The register reached 124 rows because there was always a "we will get to it", and that tier is the
   whole of why documentation outran source four to one.

The seven queued rows are not dropped, they fold into the sprints they belong to.

| Row              | Sprint | State                                                                                                                                                                             |
| ---------------- | ------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| TEST-22, TEST-24 | S0     | **closed 2026-08-01**                                                                                                                                                             |
| CON-17           | S3     | **verified, then deferred**: consequence settled and severe, reachability unestablished, and it needs a live engine to establish. Moved into the live-infrastructure block below. |
| OBS-17, OBS-18   | S2     | **closed 2026-08-01**, with batch 2. OBS-18 was already closed by CON-10 and needed a test, not a fix.                                                                            |
| CON-22, CON-23   | S3     | **closed 2026-08-01**                                                                                                                                                             |

**TEST-22 and TEST-24 went first, and the reason sharpened on the PR #49 gate.** Its Stryker run
aborted on its initial suite pass with `fetch failed` in a CON-16 test the diff never touches, after
the same 314 tests passed twice in a row locally. A relaunch got through. Under the old cadence a
flaky suite cost a retry. Under the new one everything rides on one run per sprint, so the cheaper
cadence is only safe once the suite is trustworthy. Both rows are closed: the suite now passes 8 of 8
at eight concurrent copies, against 3 of 8 before, and the bundle has assertions on its contents
rather than only on its existence.

**S0 is done. S0.3 and S0.4 stay archived**, which is deliberate rather than an omission: the two rows
this sprint plan named as S0's work were TEST-22 and TEST-24, and a coverage baseline is not on the
path to the definition of done.

**S3 is done as of 2026-08-01**, all of S3.1 through S3.7. Three of its seven rows turned out to
describe code that no longer existed or a mechanism that was wrong, which is the rate that justifies
verifying every row against the source before implementing it:

- **CON-1** was wrong about its own race. p-queue 8 runs the first job synchronously, so the two-announce
  window it describes never existed, and the real one is on the re-announce path.
- **CON-5** was fixed by CON-16 and only lacked a test that could tell.
- **CON-4** was closed by three separate earlier guards plus CON-6.
- **CON-2** needed no code at all.

S3 also produced one finding of its own, **CON-25**, a session finalized twice when a reconnect lands
mid-drain, which is CON-22's failure mode by the path CON-22's guard cannot reach.

Sprint order: **S2's seven tasks are done** as of batch 2, S2.3 through S2.7 with OBS-17 and OBS-18, but **its exit criterion is not met and the sprint is not closed**. See the note under the Sprint 2 exit. Then S1 remainder, S4 remainder, S6, S5 last,
which matches the QA-runs-last decision already in the handoff.

### Anything that needs live infrastructure is deferred to the end

Owner decision, 2026-08-01: **defer every task whose verification needs a running engine, and do them
all in one block at the end.** The reasoning is the same one behind the batched cadence. A task that
needs a live OME, a live Bee or real playback cannot be closed by `pnpm verify`, so it stalls a sprint
that is otherwise ready to land, and standing one up per task pays the setup cost over and over.

| Deferred                       | What it needs                                                                                |
| ------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **CON-17**                     | a live OME, to establish whether an unannounced media-sequence restart is reachable at all   |
| **S5.1** latency baseline      | a real end-to-end stream, since the number is the measurement                                |
| **S5.2** hls.js live retune    | real playback, since a tuning change is only as good as what it does to a real player        |
| **S6.3** bee-js spike          | a real Bee, if the evidence is to be worth anything                                          |
| The reconnect/crash/Bee-outage | a real engine, and it is the definition of done's own final clause rather than a sprint task |

**CON-17 is deferred, not archived, and the distinction is its severity.** Its consequence is settled
and severe: `OmeHlsPuller.ts` holds `segment.seq <= this.lastSeq` with no escape, so an unannounced
restart discards the new session's media forever while `/health` says `segment_stall` a window later.
What is unestablished is whether OME can produce that at all. **CON-16's measurement is not evidence
for it:** that row's own account has `startPuller` returning early on `pullers.has(streamId)`, a branch
only reached once an admission has arrived, so what was measured is the announced case CON-16 closed.
Fixing on the strength of the consequence alone has already been tried and reverted once, in `cb34d1b`.

Everything else in the plan is closable with fakes and the injected clock, so it proceeds as normal.
**Separately and permanently, not part of this deferral: on-chain actions are the owner's.** No stamp is
ever bought, extended or topped up here, on any network, so S4.6 ships its guard with `FakeBee` behind
it and the spend itself is never exercised.

### The queue this replaced

Kept because the rows are still the rows, and because the reasoning below still holds for how to order
work inside a sprint.

| Row         | Sev    | Why it is on the path to done                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| ----------- | ------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **CON-22**  | MEDIUM | **CLOSED.** The session guard disarms itself between an accepted closing and the next opening. Reconnect.                                                                                                                      |
| **CON-23**  | MEDIUM | **CLOSED.** Two sessions sharing a source port produce one key, which puts CON-21 back in full. Reconnect.                                                                                                                     |
| **CON-17**  | HIGH   | **VERIFIED in consequence, unestablished in reachability, and deferred to the live-infrastructure block.** Do not fix on the consequence alone: rewinding `lastSeq` was tried and reverted in `cb34d1b`. See its register row. |
| **OBS-17**  | MEDIUM | Nothing scrapes `/health`, and it answers `ok` at the moment a live session has been wrongly killed. Operator can tell.                                                                                                        |
| **OBS-18**  | MEDIUM | A puller that outlives its closing has one exit, a 404, which a proxy removes. Leaked puller, no VOD.                                                                                                                          |
| **TEST-22** | HIGH   | Suite reliability.                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| **TEST-24** | HIGH   | Contention scores a flaky failure as a killed mutant, so mutation numbers can lie about all of the above.                                                                                                                      |

**Severity is not the ordering.** CON-22 and CON-23 are MEDIUM and were first, because they are the
reconnect case and the definition of done names it. Several open HIGHs are archived because they are
not on this path.

### Three rules that keep it from growing back

1. **`review-gate.md` is frozen.** No edits unless a pull request is actually blocked by it. A protocol
   defect gets one archived row and the session moves on. It is a control, and a control that needs
   continuous maintenance is not controlling anything.
2. **A protocol finding is capped at MEDIUM**, unless it lets a production defect through undetected.
   The severity ladder above describes the running system, and a rule inconsistency is not silent wrong
   behaviour in the live path.
3. **A documentation-only pull request gets no lenses**, not even the claims auditor. Everything else
   gets the auditor plus one reasoning lens chosen by surface, **at the sprint boundary** rather than
   per pull request.

### What closing this looks like

The sprint plan is worked to completion, and a reconnect, a crash and a Bee outage have each been
driven end to end against a real engine with the VOD and the puller checked afterwards. That last part
is not a sprint task and is what actually proves the definition of done.

## How to read this

Every finding carries a status:

- **VERIFIED** was re-checked against the code by hand after the audit reported it. Trust these.
- **REPORTED** was found with a file:line citation but not independently re-checked. Likely, confirm
  while implementing.
- **REJECTED** items have their own section. Do not action them.

Severity ladder: CRITICAL is funds, data loss, or destruction of operator infrastructure. HIGH is
silent wrong behavior in the live path. MEDIUM is degraded behavior or real friction. LOW is polish.

## Rejected findings

Reported by an audit and did not hold up. Recorded so nobody re-opens them.

| Claim                                                                 | Why it is wrong                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **R1** Bee node passwords are committed to the repo                   | `.gitignore:12` covers `deploy/data/`, `git ls-files deploy/data` is empty, and neither file has an add-commit. Local untracked files. No leak.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| **R2** `StreamCatalog` can advance its feed index past a failed write | `retryUntilDeadlineAsync` (`utils/common.ts:69-89`) throws on exhaustion and never returns null, so `this.feedIndex = nextIndex` at `StreamCatalog.ts:115` is unreachable on failure.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| **R3** Two concurrent `addStream` calls race on `nextIndex`           | `addStream` funnels through `PQueue({ concurrency: 1 })` at `StreamCatalog.ts:31`. Single-process ordering is guaranteed. Cross-process would be real, but nothing deploys two uploaders against one stream key.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| **R4** `RecoveryStore` allows path traversal via `streamId`           | `getFilePath` (`RecoveryStore.ts:62`) replaces `/` and `\` with `_`, so no separator survives to traverse with.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| **R5** Crash recovery resurrects streams under a mangled id           | `recoverStreams` keys the live maps off `state.streamId`, not the filename (`StreamOrchestrator.ts:173`), with a comment naming exactly this trap.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| **R6** `persistState` is an unawaited async call                      | It is synchronous inside a try/catch (`StreamUploader.ts:233-239`). The consequence, a swallowed persist failure leaving stale recovery state, is real and tracked as OBS-4. The mechanism is not.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| **R7** hls.js needs `lowLatencyMode` enabled                          | Still rejected, on a corrected reason. It already defaults to true, so setting it changes nothing, and that is the whole of why. The original reason also said it governs LL-HLS partial segments only, which is wrong: `hls.js@1.6.15` gates the playback-rate catch-up on `lowLatencyMode && maxLiveSyncPlaybackRate !== 1 && levelDetails.live` (`dist/hls.js:33530`, `dist/hls.mjs:32603`, which is the bundle Vite consumes). Reading it as unrelated is what would make someone override it to false and kill that catch-up silently. |
| **R8** Batch manifest writes through GSOC                             | GSOC is an addressing scheme for receiving messages at a known address, not a batcher for owned-feed writes. Not applicable.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| **R9** Redundancy costs "~40 BZZ per segment"                         | Not a real figure. Any redundancy decision needs a measured cost, tracked under S6.3.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |

### Rejected by the review gate on PR #24

| Claim                                                                                   | Why it is wrong                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **R10** CRITICAL: the eslint `.cjs` config lets a fork PR execute arbitrary code in CI  | CI already runs `pnpm install`, `typecheck`, `lint` and `test` against the pull request's own tree, so it executes contributor code by design. The eslint config grants nothing extra, and the proposed fix of a non-executable config format closes nothing while `pnpm test` still runs. A fork `pull_request` gets a read-only token and no secrets, and the repository default is already read-only. The one real residual, declaring `permissions` in the file, landed as `0c151c1`. |
| **R11** CRITICAL: the format job has no `set -e`, so a git failure passes as "no files" | GitHub Actions runs `run:` steps under `bash -e {0}` by default, and `bash -e` aborts on a failing command-substitution assignment. Measured: `bash -e -c 'x=$(git diff bad-ref...HEAD); echo REACHED'` exits 128 and never prints REACHED.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| **R12** `npx prettier` in CI resolves an unpinned prettier over the network             | Raised during verification rather than by a lens, and refuted the same way. prettier `^2.8.8` is a root devDependency at `package.json:38`, so after `pnpm install` npx resolves `node_modules/.bin/prettier` locally at 2.8.8.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| **R13** CRITICAL: `packages/cli` lacking eslint devDependencies makes CI fail at lint   | The consequence is false. `pnpm lint` exits 0 and CI has been green on it across Node 20 and 22. The underlying fragility is real, the package's lint depended on siblings declaring eslint, and it was fixed in `e094fe1`, but as MEDIUM latent fragility rather than a live break.                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| **R14** Restore the quoted recursive test glob `"test/**/*.test.ts"`                    | That is the exact break CI caught. `node --test` only expands glob patterns from Node 21 and the declared floor is 20, proven by run `30457803109` where node 20 failed and node 22 passed on the same commit. The directory form `tsx --test test/` also fails, measured as 1 test and 1 failure. The non-recursive form stays, with the latent gap tracked as TEST-7.                                                                                                                   |

### Rejected by the review gate on PRs #25 and #26

| Claim                                                                                               | Why it is wrong                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **R15** CRITICAL: `xargs` reports only the last invocation's exit status, so a failing batch passes | Measured on two implementations. BSD `xargs` returns 1 and busybox returns 123 when an early invocation fails and the last succeeds, so both aggregate. GNU findutils, which is what `ubuntu-latest` provides, documents exit 123 for "one or more invocations exited 1-125". The finding also asserted the repo has no `.prettierignore`, which is false: it exists and lists `node_modules`, `dist` and `pnpm-lock.yaml`.                 |

Neither `main` nor `feat/ai-hardening` has branch protection at all, both returning HTTP 404 "Branch not protected" from the API, so there are no required checks to un-gate. Worth re-checking if protection is ever added, since the concern is sound in general.                                                                                                                                          |
| **R17** MEDIUM: a tag push runs the format job against a wrong file set                             | The workflow triggers on `push: branches: ['**']`, which does not include tags. A tag push does not start this workflow at all.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| **R18** The claims lens confirming "nine declarations now agree on 22"                              | It enumerated nine and stopped, matching the author's own list, and missed the format job's `node-version`. The real count is ten, found by hand before either lens reported and corroborated by the completeness lens, whose table listed both CI locations separately. **A claims auditor can be captured by the framing of the claim it checks**, so count independently rather than testing the author's list for internal consistency. |

### Rejected by the review gate on PR #30

Six lenses ran: claims audit, correctness, security, silent failure, config consistency, test integrity.
Twenty-six findings, ten confirmed and fixed, and the rest are below. Confirmed ones are recorded against
OBS-1 and as the new rows OBS-9, OBS-10, CON-11, TEST-11 and DOC-7.

| Claim                                                                                                                                        | Why it is rejected, downgraded or deferred                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **R28** MEDIUM: the manifest failure counter resets on the re-announce path, so health flips to ok while Bee is still refusing               | Downgraded to LOW and rejected as a defect. The re-announce branch finalizes the old session and constructs a new uploader, and a new uploader genuinely has zero failures, so the count is truthful. What the finding actually describes is that `/health` has no memory across stream lifetimes, which is a property of a liveness endpoint rather than a bug in one. Counters that survive a stream are S2.7. |
| **R29** LOW: one unauthenticated `POST /stream/start` pins `/health` at 503 permanently                                                      | The endpoint is reporting the truth: a registered stream really is producing nothing. Two separate real issues sit underneath and both are recorded rather than fixed here, the missing auth as SEC-1 and S1.1, and the absent registration timeout as the new CON-11. The lens's own severity reasoning was sound, including that it escalates the moment a compose healthcheck consumes the 503.               |
| **R30** LOW: the new body fields are a feedback oracle for an attacker degrading the Swarm write path                                        | Accurate and accepted as LOW, no action. `staleManifestStreams` already exposed the same fact before this change, so the new fields refine an existing signal rather than creating one. No ids, keys, addresses or references are disclosed. Worth revisiting only when `/health` gains auth, at which point the question disappears.                                                                            |
| **R31** LOW: `queue_full` rejections past the stall window produce both `queue_pressure` and `segment_stall`, and the second reason misleads | Rejected. Both reasons are true at once: the full queue is the cause and the absence of accepted segments is its consequence. Suppressing the second would hide the fact that nothing is progressing, which is the more operationally important half. Reporting both is the intended behaviour of a reasons array.                                                                                               |
| **R32** Claims auditor, on the PR body: "all ten type errors came from one intersection because `lastSeq` is private"                        | **MISLEADING and corrected in the description.** The count of ten reproduces exactly, but only six cite `lastSeq` through `PullerInternals`. The other four cite `tick` through a different intersection, which is precisely why the fix needed two separate edits rather than one.                                                                                                                              |
| **R33** Claims auditor, on the PR body: "a scenario asserting 200 on `/health` will now fail"                                                | **UNVERIFIABLE as written, corrected in the description.** Nothing in the e2e suite reads an HTTP status code: `harness/host.ts` shells out to `curl -s` with no `-f` and parses the body. What the suite does have is four assertions on the body's `status === 'ok'`, which was a constant before this change and is now a real assertion. The corrected claim is both narrower and more useful.               |
| **R34** Test integrity: reversing the order of the `reasons` array leaves the suite green                                                    | Not a defect. Reason order is deliberately unpinned, and the one test that checks multiple reasons sorts both sides before comparing. Pinning it would freeze an implementation detail into the wire contract.                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| **R35** Test integrity: dropping the `stopStream` timestamp clear leaves the suite green                                                     | Inert rather than surviving, and the lens said so. Removing a delete from a map whose entries are only read for still-registered streams changes no observable behaviour.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |

### Rejected by the review gate on PR #38

Six lenses across two rounds. Round 1 confirmed everything it raised, which is why the fix was
reworked rather than patched, so the entries below are all from round 2 and all concern claims the
gate made about the reworked code.

| Claim                                                                                                                                                                          | Why it is wrong                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **R44** Dropping `retireSession` from the re-announce branch leaves a window in which a segment reaches the outgoing session, so the mutation surviving is a real coverage gap | The mutation survives because it is equivalent. `spawnUploader`'s queued job is synchronous and p-queue runs it inline, so all three maps are re-set before `startStream` returns and the window is zero. Probed at head and under the mutation with byte-identical output: `activeStreams` size 1, the uploader already swapped, the duplicate filter already empty, and a segment in that turn accepted in both. The claims auditor reported the opposite readings and they did not reproduce. Keeping the call is still right, because inline execution of a queued job is an implementation detail rather than a contract, but it is not something a test can hold today. |
| **R45** The retired uploader's concurrent `notifyStop` can collide with the live one on Bee feeds, the catalog, or the manifest                                                | Each uploader generates its own `streamRawTopic` with `crypto.randomUUID()`, so the `(owner, topic)` pair differs and the feeds cannot overlap. `StreamCatalog.addStream` serializes through its own `PQueue({ concurrency: 1 })` and re-reads its index inside the job, so there is no lost update. `ManifestManager` is per-uploader. Forced by the correctness lens across nine orderings including a finalize that throws and one that hangs past `DRAIN_TIMEOUT_MS`.                                                                                                                                                                                                     |

The round's own generalisable lesson is in TEST-19 rather than here: the acceptance test passed on
scheduler ordering, because a fake that resolves without yielding closes the very window the fix
targets. It is the fourth distinct way a test on this project has been green while asserting nothing.

### Rejected by the review gate on PR #43

Six lenses ran, the claims auditor first and alone. This round produced more confirmed findings than
any before it, and almost all of them were against the fix rather than against the pre-existing code,
so the table below is short: nearly everything reported was real.

| Finding                                                                                                                                                                                     | Verdict                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **R59** Concurrency lens: a late `closing` for a replaced session stops the live replacement's puller and VOD-finalizes the live session, reachable on the ordinary reconnect timeline.     | **The defect is real and is now CON-21. The stated reachability is refuted.** The scenario needs a reconnect to be admitted while the dropped session is still up, and this pull request's own measurements show OME rejects exactly that as a duplicate stream name, 4 of 4 across the boundary sweep. On the ordinary timeline both closings therefore land before the announce OME admits, and the earlier one only kills a session OME had already refused. What survives is a delayed or reordered webhook, which is a narrower condition than reported and is what the CON-21 row records. Severity kept at HIGH for that path.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| **R60** Protocol lens: the ISO 8601 representations `Date.parse` rejects (basic format, comma decimal sign, hours-only offset, ordinal and week dates) are in-spec values the parser drops. | **Correct reading of the spec, not a finding here, and the lens said so itself.** No HLS server was found that emits any of them, the RFC's own example uses the accepted form, and the captured real-OME fixture uses `+00:00`. Recorded so a later round does not re-raise it: if an origin ever does emit one, the symptom is a dropped anchor for the rest of the playlist.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| **R61** Protocol lens: `interfaces.ts` overclaims that no clock skew can enter the comparison, because a timezone-less date-time is read as host-local.                                     | **True, and corrected in the diff rather than registered.** The wording now names the exception and cites RFC 8216 section 6.3.3. Both sides of the comparison are still parsed on the same host, so a fixed offset cancels, and the lens could not make it fail.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| **R62** Test-integrity lens: 15 of 59 mutations survived.                                                                                                                                   | **Six of the fifteen are equivalent and the lens proved each one rather than asserting it, which is the standard this gate asks for and has not always got.** The nine real gaps were all acted on: six were `latestProgramDateTime` semantics and the getter is deleted, since the engine now reads its own per-stream record and nothing else called it. Deleting untestable code beats testing it.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| **R63** Author, PR #58: the first scoped mutation run is contaminated, because it scored `Logger.ts:21` survived where a hand-check kills it.                                               | **The hand-check applied a different mutation, and Stryker was right.** Stryker's `ConditionalExpression` mutator targets the operand `arg !== null` at column 37, not the whole ternary condition. `typeof arg === 'object' && true` differs from the original only when `arg` is `null`, and `String(null)` and `JSON.stringify(null)` are both `"null"`, so **no input distinguishes them**: it is an equivalent mutant. Executed over `null`, `undefined`, a string, a number, an object, an array and a boolean, with zero differing outputs. The clean re-run settles the wider claim too: **identical score of 72.93 and identical 173 survivors**, with one mutant moving between killed and timeout, which is the known structural timeout variance. **The hazard behind the claim is real and is kept**, because it is not recorded anywhere else: Stryker's sandbox symlinks `node_modules` back to the live tree, so in a pnpm workspace a package such as `packages/shared` is read live rather than from the sandbox copy, and editing one mid-run does contaminate the run. That is why the tree must be quiet, not because this particular reading proved it. |

### Rejected by the review gate on PR #46

Six lenses. Unusually few refutations, because five of the six reported against the fix rather than
against pre-existing code, and a lens reviewing a change written hours earlier is right more often
than one reviewing code it has to reconstruct. The claims auditor returned **no corrections owed at
all**, a first, which is the `pnpm gate:facts` block doing what it was built for.

- **R63.** _Mutation, `sessionKey`: `payload?.client` reduced to `payload.client` survives._ Refuted as
  equivalent. The route is mounted behind `express.json()`, which always yields an object, so
  `payload` is never nullish where this runs and the optional chain can never be the difference. Kept
  in the source as a guard against a future caller that is not the router.
- **R64.** _Mutation, `sessionKey`: forcing `typeof port === 'number'` to true survives._ Refuted as
  equivalent by construction rather than by coverage. `Number.isInteger` returns false for every
  non-number, so the following conjunct already rejects everything the removed one would have.
  Distinguishing it would need a value that is not a number and is an integer, which does not exist.
- **R65.** _Silent failure: `forget` does not bound the case its own comment names._ The lens raised it
  and refuted it in the same breath, which is the shape this section wants. The teardowns that skip
  `forget` (`onHalt`, the recovery-timeout stop, `POST /stream/stop`) leave an entry behind, but any
  later opening overwrites it and a delayed closing against a leftover key either matches and is
  honoured or differs on an already-stopped stream. A slow leak of one short string per stream id, and
  an inaccurate justification, not a behaviour fault.

**One finding of the author's own was refuted by measurement and is worth keeping**, because it was
published as fact in this document and acted on. The claim that a zero-match mutation run "reads
exactly like a mutation check that passed" is false. Stryker prints
`No files found for mutation with the given glob expressions` and then exits 0. The defect is the exit
code, not silence, and the corrected text says so. A protocol that misdiagnoses its own hole argues
for the wrong fix.

### Rejected by the review gate on PR #63

**Six lenses, none deferred, and an empty refutation table for the second round running.** 19
findings, 2 of them HIGH, and every one was confirmed. Two rounds with nothing to reject is not a
compliment to either change: it says the lenses keep finding real defects faster than this side
produces false ones.

**The mutation check was unavailable rather than not applicable.** The harness covers
`packages/stream-uploader` and this diff is entirely `packages/client`, so no Stryker run happened
and there is no `Found N of M file(s) to be mutated` line to quote. That is the answer, not an
omission. **PR #62's mutation-triage deferral does not clear here**, because its surface is the
uploader's source.

**Three defects were found independently by three lenses each**, with the same fix: an answered 404
never ending a run of gateway failures, the eviction path changing state without publishing, and the
playback-rate guard never reading the rate already on the element. Convergence at that rate is the
strongest signal this gate produces, and it is worth recording that all three came from _different_
questions rather than from three lenses asking one.

**One severity was downgraded rather than accepted, under R2.** The concurrency lens rated MEDIUM a
case where a follow-up failure from a torn-down generation lands after the replacement mount's
initial fetch has already succeeded, putting a healthy mount into `reconnecting` with a 2 second
hold. Confirmed as a defect and downgraded to LOW, because the fix for the converged 404 finding
bounds it: any answered poll now ends the failure run, and the follow-up path polls about once per
target duration, so the wrong state survives one backoff interval rather than indefinitely. Filed as
`CON-33` rather than fixed here, since the honest fix needs a per-topic answer counter and the
residual harm is a two second overlay flash.

**Nothing was refuted.** The next `R` id remains 74.

## Deferred lenses

A lens the surface selected, that did not run before the merge, under
[what blocks a merge](./review-gate.md#what-blocks-a-merge-and-what-only-files-a-row). **Exactly two
lenses may appear here, mutation triage and test integrity.** Anything else in this table is a rule
violation rather than a deferral.

It lives in the register rather than in a pull request comment because of who has to find it. A
comment is permanent and checkable by a reader already looking at that pull request, and the reader
this exists for is a later session that does not know which pull requests to open. That is the same
reason R5 built a register instead of trusting the timeline.

**A row closes when a later round runs that lens on the same surface**, which is the next pull request
touching it. **The S3 gate on 2026-08-01 is the first sprint exit this project has reached**, and it
cleared the only open row. **An open row here fails the sprint exit gate**, which is enumerated in
[the handoff](./2026-07-29-hardening-handoff.md) as its single home.

| PR  | Lens            | Surface                        | Deferred on | Cleared by                                    |
| --- | --------------- | ------------------------------ | ----------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| #47 | Test integrity  | `tests`                        | `3ac0540`   | **closed at the S3 gate, PR #51, 2026-08-01** |
| #62 | Mutation triage | `packages/stream-uploader/src` | `347c35f`   | **open**                                      |

**The #62 row was owed and is filed late.** Its posted result said the ledger row would follow and no
row was written, which is the failure this table exists to make visible and instead demonstrated on
itself. The run did not defer: 1134 mutants, 664 killed, 148 timed out, 322 survived, score 71.60%,
and those numbers are in the PR #62 result. What deferred is the triage of the 322, because the branch
was rewritten in response to the same gate and survivors of a head that no longer exists would produce
findings against code that has changed. `StreamCatalog.ts` at 47.22% with zero timeouts is the file to
start from. **PR #63 does not clear it**, because it touches `packages/client` and the surface here is
the uploader's source.

**What clearing it produced**, since a row cleared by assertion is not cleared: 109 mutations over the
S3 diff, 82 killed, 27 survivors triaged to nine findings, of which four were HIGH. The sharpest is
worth carrying because it is the shape this whole table exists to catch: the keepalive-activity test
asserted nothing at all, and replacing the entire code path it named with a `throw` still passed it.

**Why the S3 gate and not PR #49.** PR #49 does touch `tests`, which under the rule below is what
clears a row, and it did not clear this one: its surface selected concurrency, and one reasoning lens
per pull request is the rule. Under the cadence decided the same day the lens round runs once per
sprint over the whole sprint diff, so this row clears at the S3 gate by construction rather than by
whichever pull request happens to touch the surface next. That also removes the deferral mechanism's
reason to exist going forward, since a sprint gate runs the full catalogue and has nothing to defer to.

**About that row.** PR #47 changes `test/OmeEngine.test.ts`, including the contract of its `waitFor`
helper, which now throws where it used to return. That is squarely test integrity's surface. It was
deferred under the rule the same pull request introduces, which is either the rule working as intended
or the first instance of the drift it is designed to prevent, and only the round that clears it will
say which. The mutation triage half did **not** defer: the Stryker run is blocking, it ran, and its
numbers are in the posted result.

The mechanism is worth writing down because it defeats the obvious test: `spawnUploader` hands the work to a `PQueue` with `concurrency: 1`, and p-queue runs a job inline when the queue is idle, so `activeStreams.set` overwrites the stale entry in the same synchronous turn that `retireSession` would have deleted it. All three maps `retireSession` clears are re-set by `spawnUploader`, so under an idle queue the call is redundant and the surviving mutant genuinely is equivalent. It stops being equivalent the moment a queued job is not inline, which is exactly when the CON-16 window reopens. So this is defence in depth with no test holding it rather than dead code: do not delete it, cover it. A test needs the queue busy across the re-announce, and no current test can arrange that, because every job the orchestrator queues is synchronous. | OBS-1  | CRITICAL | CLOSED   | `api/routes/health.ts:10`                                                                                                                         | `status` is the string literal `'ok'`. The first of those closed it only partially and the review gate on PR #30 caught the rest, so the closure is worth reading as four fixes rather than one. `deriveHealthStatus` degrades on three consecutive live-manifest publish failures, on high queue pressure, or on a registered stream silent for `SEGMENT_STALL_MS`, and degraded answers 503. All four states are proven end to end over HTTP. The threshold is three rather than one because a failed publish is retried at the same SOC index on the next segment, so one or two self-heal and would only flap the endpoint. Then, from the gate: a refused **segment** upload was invisible to all three original signals at once, which is the most likely real failure of the lot, so consecutive segment failures became a fourth signal at a threshold of one. The stall clock was one process-wide scalar, so any live stream masked a dead sibling. A normal drain and every crash recovery both reported degraded, because a draining stream stays registered while accepting nothing and `RECOVERY_TIMEOUT` is twice the stall window. All four are fixed and each is pinned by a mutation that fails exactly its own test. | OBS-2  | CRITICAL | CLOSED   | `OmeHlsPuller.ts`, client `ManifestManagement.ts`, `providers/App.tsx`, `components/StreamPreview/StreamPreview.tsx`, `utils/fetchWithTimeout.ts` | Four bare `fetch()` calls with no timeout or abort. Node's fetch has no default timeout, so a black-holed connection stalls the puller indefinitely while health reports ok. **Uploader half closed** by `a4c7149`: all three puller calls route through one `fetchWithTimeout` using a fresh `AbortSignal.timeout`, settable with `OME_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS` and defaulting to 10s, and an abort logs at error level so it is distinguishable from an ordinary failure. **Two corrections to this row.** The count of four is low: `client/src/providers/App.tsx:66` is a fifth bare `fetch` this row never named, since the four it does name are the three puller calls plus `ManifestManagement.ts:279`, and `client/src/components/StreamPreview/StreamPreview.tsx:48` carries an unmount `AbortSignal` but no timeout, so it hangs just as long. Neither was in the original list. **Client half closed** by `64cefb6`, three sites rather than one: `ManifestManagement.fetchResource`, `App.tsx`'s app-state poll, and `StreamPreview`, which carried an unmount signal and no timeout so it hung just as long. `fetchWithTimeout` composes the caller's signal rather than replacing it, so an unmount still aborts work in flight, and reports a timeout as its own error type so a silent gateway is distinguishable from a cancelled render. **Built from `AbortController` and `setTimeout` on purpose.** `AbortSignal.timeout` and `AbortSignal.any` are the obvious tools and are both newer than the bundle's declared `build.target`: `AbortSignal.timeout` arrives in Safari 16 against a target of Safari 14, so it would throw at runtime on exactly the engines the target promises and nothing in the build would say so. The timeout is tracked with a local flag rather than an abort reason for the same reason. See TEST-22 for why a build that succeeds says nothing about what is in the bundle. **The uploader's guarantee could not be reproduced here.** There it routes every call through one helper so a new call site cannot forget the window. Any client component can reach for the global instead, so the equivalent is asserted rather than designed in: a test fails if any call to the global `fetch` remains in `src`. Six mutations, each killed, three of them being each site reverted to a bare fetch. **The first version of that helper was wrong and shipped inside this row's own fix.** `fetch` resolves at the response headers and the body is a separate stream read afterwards, so clearing the timer and unsubscribing the caller's signal on return bounded only the time to headers: a gateway answering 200 and then withholding the body hung the caller with no window left to stop it. Measured against a real stalling server, a 300ms window was still hanging at 2000ms. **It was a regression, not merely a gap:** `StreamPreview` previously passed its unmount signal straight to `fetch`, where it did abort the body read, and the control proving that is in the same measurement. Worse there than one preview, because the thumbnail queue runs at concurrency 1, so one stuck read blocks every thumbnail for the life of the page. | OPS-1  | CRITICAL | CLOSED   | `cli/commands/stamp-setup.ts:86-110`, `lib/env-writer.ts:7-8` | The batch id is written to `.env` **after** the on-chain spend, and `writeEnvKey` throws ENOENT when `.env` is missing. A fresh clone spends BZZ and then crashes with the batch id only in scrollback. **Closed** by `63fb99a` and `10a9cb3`. Three separate ways to lose the id, all shut. `writeEnvKey` creates the file instead of throwing ENOENT. The recording moved to immediately after `buyStamp` returns, with nothing that can throw in between, where `waitForStamp` used to sit and routinely times out. A writability preflight refuses the spend outright when the result cannot be recorded, saying so, which is the outcome that costs nothing. The preflight cannot close the check-to-write race, so `recordBatchId` degrades from `.env` to a recovery file beside it to one in the temp directory, and the id is echoed whatever happens. The command no longer reports a successful `.env` write when the write failed. Both halves of the acceptance criterion are covered by tests that drive the real `stampSetup` through injected seams, and both were mutation-checked. The cli package had no test harness at all before this, so `pnpm verify` was reporting success while running nothing here: that is `0126609`. No real purchase was made at any point. **Gate round 1 found the first fix incomplete in five ways, all now closed.** The ordering was never an independent loss path: the base had a second write inside the wait's own catch, so a timeout alone still recorded the id when `.env` existed and was writable. It became a loss only combined with `writeEnvKey` throwing. More seriously, the fix introduced three new defects. A spend whose id never reached `.env` **exited 0 and ended by telling the operator to deploy**. The wait-timeout branch claimed the id was "already recorded" without inspecting the record, in a run that had just said it could not be saved anywhere. The reuse path, where nothing is bought, announced the batch was "PAID FOR". Separately, `writeFileSync` truncates before writing, so a write failing partway destroyed STREAM_KEY, API_AUTH_TOKEN and the rest with nothing in the output saying so: now an atomic sibling-and-rename. And `pnpm stamp:buy` spends through the same call and recorded nothing at all, so scoping this row to `stamp:setup` would have been a dodge: it is fixed too. | LAT-1 | HIGH   | CLOSED   | whole pipeline                                  | No glass-to-glass latency instrumentation exists, so no latency change can currently be proven. This blocks every other LAT item from being measurable. **CLOSED 2026-08-03: the instrument exists and the baseline is measured.** Against the `latbench` deployment on manager-host, engine SRS, 1280x720 @ 30fps 2500kbps 2s GOP, five segments sampled: **capture to fetchable 5.94s median** (range 4.21s to 7.60s), and **13.30s behind live** for a viewer, with the client's configured 10s `liveSyncDuration`. Behind-live is deliberately not total-plus-buffer: the total is anchored on a segment's first frame and the buffer is measured back from the live edge, which is that same segment's last, so adding them counts one segment twice. The review gate on PR #64 caught that, and the figure first published here was 15.94s. Report at `docs/bench/latency-2026-08-02T16-14-48-385Z.md`. It publishes with `-use_wallclock_as_timestamps 1 -copyts` so each frame carries the bench machine's clock, then ffprobes the fetched segment's first frame, with no OCR anywhere. The publisher and the gateway fetch both run on the bench machine, so no clock skew enters the total; the two hops bounded by an uploader log line carry it instead, and it cancels between them. A reading is bounded by the only two facts that hold by construction, that a frame cannot be captured before the publisher started nor fetched before it was captured, so an engine that rebases timestamps on repackage is reported as unmeasurable rather than turned into a plausible number. A local self-check publishes, probes and recovers the whole chain offline before a run spends any postage, and it earned its place immediately: the first real run failed it, because the publisher stalled outright about half the time until `-re` was replaced by the `realtime` filters (see the commit for the measurements). **The per-hop split inside that total is not sound yet, see LAT-9.** The total is, because it is bounded end to end by the bench's own clock and no other. The knob sweep is deliberately not built yet, because each cell costs a real broadcast and a matrix over an unvalidated measurement is money spent on numbers nobody should trust. |

Clock skew is not the cause: it was measured independently at 162ms with the host ahead, over four round trips, against the 184ms the run itself estimated, and correcting it moves the hop by 22ms. What is left is the segment-duration model. `run.ts:176` takes `segmentDuration(newest.extinf)` from whichever entry is newest at poll time and attributes it to the sampled segment, and `split.ts:96` then places the segment's close at `capturedAtMs + that duration`, which for these runs lands after the upload was already logged. Both packages' local type modules became re-exports, so the twenty-odd import sites kept their paths. **The round trip is ten tests in the uploader**, building with its own `ManifestManager` and reading back with the function the client player calls: URIs in order, durations exact including fractional ones, the discontinuity on the segment that follows it, VOD finalized and live not, the live window, and an empty manifest. Uploader 483 to 493, shared 30 new. **One definition also made a rename invisible**, since both sides move together and still agree with each other while emitting something no player accepts, so the tag spellings are pinned against RFC 8216 as literals in shared's own test. Five reverts, each failing only its arm: a renamed `HLS_EXTINF` fails the pin, a discontinuity emitted after its segment fails the round trip and the existing discontinuity test, and **rounding a duration or dropping `ENDLIST` fails the round trip alone**, which is what the ten tests were added for. The package is source-only, with `exports` pointing at the TypeScript entry, so tsx, vitest and tsc consume it with no build step and CI's test-before-build order is untouched. **The uploader's build gained a vendor step** because the production image copies `dist/` and runs `npm install --omit=dev` against the uploader's manifest alone, where a `workspace:*` dependency has nowhere to come from: shared compiles into `dist/node_modules`, which node's resolution walk finds from `dist/index.js` and `dist/utils/env.js` alike, and it is a devDependency so `--omit=dev` correctly skips it. Bundling was rejected for a specific reason: `src/utils/env.ts` resolves the repository root by walking four levels up from its own compiled location, so collapsing `dist/utils/env.js` into `dist/index.js` moves the `.env` it reads with no error anywhere. | ARCH-3 | MEDIUM | CLOSED   | `StreamUploader.ts`, `libs/AnnounceReadiness.ts`, `StreamOrchestrator.ts` `recoverStreams`               | The stream lifecycle is encoded in six loose booleans and counters with no documented legal transitions. **CLOSED 2026-08-02** by `19bfa4e` and `1e3f91a`, after being **re-scoped against source, because as written the row is half stale and half imprecise.** The lifecycle it names **already exists**: `StreamLifecycle` (live, draining, finalized, failed, unknown) is in `types.ts` and `StreamOrchestrator` and the stream route both use it, added by the sprint 3 CON work after this row was filed. And the six fields at what is now `:68-75` are not one lifecycle: `liveManifestQueued` is a queue dedupe latch, `pendingDiscontinuity` is content state, and the two `consecutive*Failures` are health counters. **What is genuinely an undocumented state machine is the announce readiness**, `isFirstSegmentReady` and `isFirstManifestReady`, which progress false/false at `:68-69`, to segment-ready at `:166`, to announced at `:418`, and are read as a gate at `:390`. **The illegal combination is announced-without-a-segment**, and it has exactly one way in: `restoreState` at `:119-120` assigns both straight from a persisted recovery entry with no validation. In that state the `:390` gate can never fire, so `announceToCatalog` is never called and the stream is never published, which makes a recovered broadcast invisible to every viewer with nothing logged. Two booleans holding three legal states is what makes the fourth representable at all. **A guard cannot simply throw from the constructor**: `recoverStreams` at `:437-458` builds each uploader inside a bare `for` loop with no try/catch, so one unparseable entry would abort recovery of every stream behind it. Isolating the loop body per stream is a prerequisite for the guard rather than a separate nicety, and is worth doing on its own. **The fix, in that order.** `19bfa4e` moves the rebuild into `recoverStream` and catches per entry, proven by a state whose segment list did not survive the disk, corrupt in a way the body reaches _after_ the uploader is constructed, so the isolation has to cover the whole rebuild. `1e3f91a` replaces the pair with one `AnnounceReadiness`, and restoring the impossible combination throws. **The persisted shape is unchanged** so older entries still load, asserted against literals rather than through the round trip, which would pass just as happily on a format nothing else can read. **The two events are modelled as events rather than as target states**, because both call sites run on every segment and not only the first, so `onFirstSegmentUploaded` must be idempotent or the second segment of every broadcast that had already announced is a move backwards. Uploader 493 to 509. Both proven by reverting the change and watching only the guarded test fail. **One process note**: the first control run reported the new test passing without the guard, which was wrong. `git stash push` with a pathspec naming an untracked file stashes nothing, and the `pop` that followed restored an unrelated stash from a branch abandoned weeks ago, conflicting two register files. Nothing was lost, but the reading was garbage. Back up the file and use `git checkout HEAD --` for a control run, never `git stash`. |     |
| ARCH-4 | LOW    | CLOSED   | `libs/Logger.ts`, `libs/logLevels.ts`                                                                    | Logger writes straight to console with no level control and no structured output. **CLOSED 2026-08-02** by `62ef50d`. `LOG_LEVEL` suppresses by threshold and a suppressed call never reaches the formatter, so a level nobody prints costs no timestamp and no `JSON.stringify` per segment. `LOG_FORMAT=json` emits one `{ts, level, msg}` object per line. The sink is replaceable, so tests read what was written rather than spying on `console`. **The levels rank `log` below `info`**, because that is how the service already uses them, per-segment against per lifecycle event, and ranking them apart is what makes `LOG_LEVEL=info` drop a line per segment for every live stream while keeping the ones that say what the service did. **The default is `debug`**, so this changes what a deployment prints by exactly nothing: turning the volume down is an operator's decision and belongs in a change that says so. An unusable value is reported and ignored rather than thrown, since a typo in the log volume should not be an outage, and the rejection goes out at `error`, which every threshold admits, so the message saying the setting was rejected cannot be suppressed by the setting. **Both variables also had to be added to the compose environment block**, which enumerates rather than inherits: a variable absent there is one the container never sees however carefully an operator sets it in `.env`, so documenting them in `.env.sample` alone would have shipped a dead setting. Uploader 509 to 528.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |

Layering itself is clean. The audit found no dependency-direction violations, and the engine plugin
boundary holds. The problems are at the package seams and in testability, not in the shape.

Measured by the correctness lens, each with an executed input. It requires the media URI on the line immediately after its `#EXTINF`, so anything RFC 8216 permits in between takes **the segment** with it rather than only itself: a blank line (§4.1 says ignore them) drops the segment silently, and `#EXT-X-BYTERANGE`, which §4.3.2.2 requires to sit exactly there, makes a whole byte-range playlist parse to **zero segments while still reading as finalized**. A dropped segment also consumes the pending discontinuity rather than passing it on, so the marker vanishes instead of moving and the surviving segment is announced as continuous across a break the source declared. Separately, `segmentDuration` uses `Number.parseFloat`, which stops at the first unusable character: `#EXTINF:6abc,` reads 6, `#EXTINF:-6,` reads -6 where RFC requires a positive number, and **`#EXTINF:0x10,` reads 0**, which is the one that matters because it makes an unparseable duration indistinguishable from a real zero-length segment, exactly the confusion the function's own test says it exists to prevent. The JSDoc now states these limits rather than implying RFC coverage. **Not fixed here**, because every one of them changes what the client player accepts and belongs in a change that says so. Pinning the target index at call time is the correctness fix, and mutation says either half prevents the skip alone, since removing the re-entry guard alone and un-pinning alone are both equivalent mutants. The guard earns its place for a different reason, which is that it stops several polls asking for the same slot at once and removes an interleaving where a late callback drags the index backwards and forces a re-fetch. The 404 handling came with it and is asserted. The shorter timeout did not, because `fetchWithTimeout` has since made 10s the default for every client request, which is the value that pull request chose. ## Why Sprint 0 exists

Two structural facts gate everything else.

**The repo had no CI.** That is why a prettier violation shipped inside PR #10 and sat there
unnoticed. A plan whose acceptance criteria are tests is worthless if nothing runs the tests on push.
**Closed by S0.1**, which added `.github/workflows/ci.yml` and caught a real latent break on its first
run, a test glob that had never worked on the declared minimum Node version.

**Roughly half the acceptance criteria below are currently unwritable.** There is no way to make Bee
return a 402, no way to advance the clock deterministically for the 60-second recovery timer or the
5-minute drain timeout, no way to substitute `fetch` in `OmeHlsPuller`, and no HTTP-level test layer.
Sprint 0 buys the ability to prove the rest, and without it the re-check loop degrades into re-reading
the diff.

## Sprint plan

One fix per commit. One PR per task. Conventional commit subjects. Every PR goes through the Copilot
gate described below.
